CASE REPORT

STIFF PERSON SYNDROME WITH ATYPICAL FEATURES AND A FAVOURABLE
OUTCOME WITH STEROIDS
Here we describe a male patient with stiff person syndrome
A forty year old male patient

A forty year old male patient with complaints of difficulty of swallowing, generalised muscle spasms and generalised seizures was admitted to our clinic. His complaints began 3 months before his admission.

extractions.value: Patient had a sequela of poliomyelitis affecting his left lower extremity. He also reported an aura like feeling preceding the spasmodic attacks. Muscle strength in the left lower extremity was 3/5. EEG was normal. Patient had generalised tonic clonic seizures as an atypical feature of SPS. Pyramidal signs (bilateral increased biceps reflexes, extensor plantar reflexes) were present.
